chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Hayy, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who was found murdered. Then two men came to his guardian, and one of them said: “I killed him intentionally,” while the other said: “I killed him by mistake.”

He عليه السلام said: “If he accepts the statement of the one who confessed to intentional killing, then he has no claim against the one who confessed to accidental killing. And if he accepts the statement of the one who confessed to accidental killing, then he has no claim against the one who confessed to intentional killing.”

key_terms.خَطَأً: by mistake; accidental killing in the legal sense
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْخَطَإِ: the one claiming responsibility for accidental killing
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْعَمْدِ: the one claiming responsibility for intentional killing
key_terms.عَمْدًا: intentionally; deliberate killing in the legal sense
key_terms.وَلِيِّهِ: the legal guardian of the victim who holds the right to pursue the claim

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if two men confess to the same killing, one intentionally and one by mistake?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a murdered person when two different men separately confess, one to intentional killing and the other to accidental killing. The victim’s guardian must proceed on the basis of one confession, and once he does so, he has no claim against the other confessor. The narration is significant in fiqh because it addresses conflicting admissions in a homicide case and limits legal liability accordingly.
